title: Fine Windows controls
summary: Observation-scoped Windows UIA tools with opaque refs and concrete policy checks.

tools.name: desktop_windows
tools.title: Windows on Windows
tools.description: List allowed Windows applications and opaque window choice IDs. Select one in desktop_snapshot.

tools.name: desktop_snapshot
tools.title: Snapshot on Windows
tools.description: Read the hierarchical UIA tree with fresh Windows refs. window is a choice_id from desktop_windows; omit to reuse this run's window. Old refs expire on the next published snapshot or any effect. Password values are hidden.

tools.name: desktop_applications
tools.title: Installed Windows applications
tools.description: List fixed, installed and allowed application IDs. Use an ID with desktop_open_application; no path, arguments, document or URL is accepted.

tools.name: desktop_open_application
tools.title: Open installed Windows application
tools.description: Open one reviewed application from desktop_applications. PANINI requires a new native window before claiming success; no path or arguments are accepted.

tools.name: desktop_click
tools.title: Click on Windows
tools.description: Click a fresh ref, invoking a supported control pattern or paced pointer input. Permissions use the actual current label; changed targets are refused.

tools.name: desktop_type
tools.title: Type on Windows
tools.description: Set an editable field value, or type plain Unicode text into a document. replace=true selects and replaces the whole document in the same grounded control. Document Enter/Tab must be separate reviewed desktop_press steps. Credentials are never typed. Snapshot and verify afterward.

tools.name: desktop_select
tools.title: Select on Windows
tools.description: Select a visible selection-item ref, or the uniquely named visible option under a list ref. Open closed lists and snapshot first.

tools.name: desktop_toggle
tools.title: Toggle on Windows
tools.description: Toggle a control with a native toggle pattern. Current label determines policy. Assert the resulting state.

tools.name: desktop_scroll
tools.title: Scroll on Windows
tools.description: Scroll a visible native scroll-pattern container. Take a new snapshot afterward.

tools.name: desktop_press
tools.title: Press on Windows
tools.description: Press one key or a Ctrl/Shift/Alt/Win chord into the unique focused control. Enter, Save, delete and system shortcuts receive their concrete effect classes. Password focus is refused.

tools.name: desktop_verify_text
tools.title: Verify text on Windows
tools.description: Assert that text appears in a fresh accessible name or value. Returns explicit assertion evidence.

tools.name: desktop_verify_value
tools.title: Verify value on Windows
tools.description: Assert a fresh text-field value for a ref from the latest snapshot, uniquely matching the same role, name and bounds. Credential values are refused.

tools.name: desktop_verify_element
tools.title: Verify element on Windows
tools.description: Assert that an element with exact accessible role and name is visible in a fresh tree. An optional current ref binds the assertion to that element's anchor.

tools.name: desktop_focus
tools.title: Focus on Windows
tools.description: Focus one non-credential control from the latest snapshot without invoking or clicking it. Snapshot afterward and verify focused_ref before pressing keys.

tools.name: desktop_activate
tools.title: Activate window on Windows
tools.description: Bring one explicitly selected allowed window to the foreground without clicking or invoking any control. The current window title and application are reviewed; snapshot afterward before using refs. This is an input action, never a side effect of observation.

principles: Windows: desktop_applications lists reviewed fixed app IDs; desktop_open_application requires owner review and a verified new window. Then desktop_windows and desktop_activate(window=choice_id) select a window. desktop_snapshot observes only; it never activates a window. Use only fresh refs and verify after every action.
Press requires a unique focused non-credential control. Credentials are always reserved for the person. Never guess a ref, window ID or native UIA ID.
Fine desktop tools are opt-in. The coarse drawing planner remains available for canvas tasks.
